P001.text: Act on folder records and handoff histories, where unresolved metadata questions, rights requests, or failed transfers may leave traces that scanning totals do not reveal.

P002.text: These traces are possible diagnostic residues, not established causes of the reported backlog.

P003.text: Assume folders can be linked across stages by identifier; verify this before interpreting counts.

P004.text: Treat exhibition readiness as requiring the museum’s agreed metadata and rights evidence, which must first be specified.

P005.text: Apply an evidence-reconciliation probe: for each sampled folder, compare its recorded stage with dated review decisions, outstanding questions, rights evidence, and handoff acknowledgments.

P006.text: Ask the relevant reviewer to resolve each discrepancy against those records; unresolved traces trigger a localized flag identifying the folder, stage, missing evidence, and next action.

P007.text: Propose a budget of 20 randomly selected histories, distributed across recorded stages and available size, completeness, and queue-age groups; record selection probabilities and unavailable histories.

P008.text: Examine up to five additional suspicious histories separately without using them to estimate prevalence.

P009.text: Each day, reconcile stage arrivals, completions, returns, and remaining queues, alongside actual volunteer hours.

P010.text: Preserve original histories and log probe-generated changes separately.

P011.text: Stop examining a history when its evidence is reconciled or a predefined time allowance expires; label expired or inaccessible cases inconclusive.

P012.text: If identifiers or stage definitions cannot be reconciled, repair that measurement problem before projecting completion.

P013.text: Observe whether reconciliation produces a flag that routine totals lacked: for example, a recorded review completion without the required decision, an unanswered rights request, or a transfer without acknowledgment.

P014.text: These are proposed signal types, not observed findings.

P015.text: Record each flag’s location, supporting trace, age, and disposition; distinguish confirmed unresolved work, explained discrepancies, and inconclusive cases. Also observe daily queue changes, rework, and completion per staffed hour within comparable folder groups. A probe-triggered resolution is an intervention and must be recorded separately from evidence of the prior state.

P016.text: A supported flag warrants concluding that the specified folder contains evidence of unresolved or inconsistently recorded work at that location.

P017.text: It does not establish why the delay occurred.

P018.text: Use recurring supported flags, queue growth, and measured effort to propose the next two weeks of assignments: allocate suitably trained volunteers to the demonstrated metadata or rights constraint, assign owners to external dependencies, and limit additional scanning where it only increases waiting inventory.

P019.text: Respect actual volunteer availability and required rights authority.

P020.text: Produce a range of ten-week readiness estimates using stage-specific throughput, folder mix, remaining work, and scheduled hours; use only the probability sample for prevalence estimates, with appropriate weighting and uncertainty.

P022.text: If even the optimistic supported estimate falls below the promised scope, propose reducing or changing that scope promptly.

P023.text: If the estimate range crosses the promise, identify a contingent reduced scope and gather targeted evidence before the week-two decision.

P024.text: Count only folders meeting the agreed readiness criteria toward the exhibition.

P025.text: Legitimate holds, stale status fields, duplicate records, or undocumented completed work may produce the same flags as unresolved work.

P026.text: Missing, overwritten, sparse, or inaccessible histories may conceal relevant traces, so no flag does not establish readiness.

P027.text: A limited sample may miss rare, difficult folders; aggregate counts can conceal size differences, and scanning rates cannot substitute for metadata or rights capacity.

P028.text: Throughput projections remain conditional on staffing, folder mix, rework, and external rights responses; widen ranges or withhold a defensible scope forecast when these inputs are inadequate.

P029.text: Flags do not establish negligence, the original delaying event, or legal clearance.

P030.text: Reconciliation may consume scarce reviewer time, prompt work, or alter records needed for later diagnosis.

P031.text: Retain dated snapshots, cap probe effort, and refer unresolved rights decisions to an authorized decision-maker before inclusion.
